study type: Multiple methods program evaluation with a quasi-experimental pre/post comparison
exposure: Virtual care for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM)
outcome: Patient experience (satisfaction, money saved, time saved, preference for virtual visits)
cohort: The study included 85 women receiving GDM care who completed patient experience surveys and 6 health-care providers at a Diabetes in Pregnancy Clinic who were interviewed.
finding: Virtual GDM care achieved high patient and provider satisfaction, resulted in cost and time savings for patients, and reduced missed appointments, while showing no significant differences in most clinical outcomes compared to in-person care.
mod_finding: There were no significant differences in rates of cesarean section procedures between in-person and virtual GDM care.
cross-section timing: Clinical outcomes were compared before (April 2019 to February 2020) and after (May 2020 to March 2021) the shift to virtual care.
birth_weight: Macrosomia was an outcome, which is defined by birth weight.
